{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVMWpgs8AAAABZXVLMQ", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BnW-xzhC-oec", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BnW-x", "number": 31, "title": "Add a 256 KiB MSX2 RAM mapper with FCh–FFh banking", "body": "## Problem

MSX2 currently provides fixed 64 KiB RAM in slot 3-3. Mapper-port reads return FFh and writes do nothing. Software cannot select RAM segments or access memory above 64 KiB, blocking workloads that require mapped RAM.

## Expected outcome

Provide one fixed 256 KiB MSX2 RAM mapper in the existing slot 3-3: sixteen shared 16 KiB segments, independently selectable for each CPU page through FCh–FFh. Preserve MSX1's fixed 64 KiB RAM and existing firmware, cartridge, audio, disk, SRAM and browser behavior.

## Context

- Inspected main: `2596b4eb2e824e6f7d8b783d0f2aaed5f14803f1`. `Hardware` in `crates/msx-core/src/lib.rs` allocates 65,536 RAM bytes, indexes them directly and has no mapper I/O decoding. Existing slot tests cover fixed RAM only.
- No open Issues or PRs were found. Earlier #11/#12 introduced MSX2; #27/#28 implemented cartridge mappers and SRAM. This task addresses system RAM banking.
- The [MSX2 Technical Handbook I/O map](https://github.com/Konamiman/MSX2-Technical-Handbook/blob/master/md/Appendix6.md) assigns FCh–FFh to the mapper. [openMSX mapper behavior](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/openMSX/openMSX/master/src/memory/MSXMemoryMapperBase.cc) documents page translation, capacity masking, register readback and reset selectors of zero. Readback/reset vary among hardware implementations; the contract below selects one supported profile rather than claiming universality.
- [Upstream C-BIOS CHKRAM](https://github.com/cbios/cbios/blob/master/src/main.asm) initializes page selectors to 3,2,1,0. Validate the bundled 0.29a binaries through execution; keep their bytes unchanged. The repository's original loaders currently omit mapper initialization.
- `msx_disk_boot_state` in `crates/msx-wasm/src/lib.rs` directly reads physical `ram[0xf104]`; it must observe the mapped logical address. Existing tests also assume physical offsets equal CPU addresses.
- Inspected [PR #30 CI](https://github.com/takahirox/msx-rust/actions/runs/39589309521) actually records 115 Rust tests and 82 browser tests passing. These establish existing behavior, with no RAM-mapper coverage. No suites were rerun for this handoff, and no commercial-title compatibility is established.

## Pre-merge acceptance

- [ ] Implement the fixed profile: FCh/FDh/FEh/FFh select pages 0000h–3FFFh/4000h–7FFFh/8000h–BFFFh/C000h–FFFFh. Decode the low port byte consistently with existing I/O. Store selector bits 0–3; ignore bits 4–7; return `F0h | selected_segment`. Address translation is `segment * 4000h + page_offset`. I/O operates even while the RAM slot is hidden; memory accesses still obey primary/secondary slot selection.
- [ ] Preserve ROM protection, unmapped reads and the expanded-slot register's precedence at memory address FFFFh. Distinguish that address from I/O port FFh. MSX1 must retain its current memory and unconnected mapper-port behavior.
- [ ] Reset all four selectors to zero before firmware execution. Make original MSX2 Weave BASIC, diagnostic and disk loaders establish 3,2,1,0 through emulated Z80 I/O before depending on separate RAM pages. Keep assembly documentation consistent with generated bytes. C-BIOS and supplied firmware perform their own initialization; introduce no native BIOS bypass or firmware-specific mapper reset values. Preserve existing RAM clearing, in-place reset and transactional import guarantees.
- [ ] Audit physical-RAM consumers, including Wasm disk boot status. Update logical observations and affected tests to follow mapping; do not preserve flat-layout assumptions by weakening banking. Failed imports must preserve active selectors, RAM, firmware, media and unsaved cartridge SRAM.
- [ ] Add independent Rust coverage through bus operations for all sixteen segments, all four pages, shared-segment aliasing, independent selectors, segment wrapping/readback, page boundaries, hidden-slot I/O, slot isolation, FFFFh precedence and pre-execution reset. Include an alias-based capacity probe that establishes sixteen distinct segments without relying on register readback or backing-vector length.
- [ ] Add an original Z80 cartridge probe that banks memory above 64 KiB and reports observable success/failure. Exercise it through bundled C-BIOS and the normal browser ROM picker at both `/` and `/msx-rust/`, including Reset. Cover supplied-firmware initialization using authored firmware, and preserve original-loader boot, disk boot/status/read/write/export, MSX1/MSX2 switching, BASIC, audio, input, cartridge/SRAM lifecycle and failed-import regressions. Replace affected raw-memory assertions with valid logical observations.
- [ ] Update README and MSX2 profile documentation with capacity, slot, selectors, masking/readback, reset versus firmware initialization and remaining limits. Implement independently from documented behavior; preserve existing licenses/provenance. Keep multiple mappers, configurable machine profiles and disk-firmware expansion outside this task.
- [ ] The Coordinator must run and report `cargo fmt --all -- --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace --locked`, `./scripts/build.sh`, `node scripts/check-dist.mjs` and `npm test`, installing browser dependencies as documented when needed. Complete repository review and resolve blocking findings before merge. Distinguish passed, failed, skipped and unperformed checks. Proprietary ROMs, physical hardware and human gameplay are unnecessary acceptance prerequisites.

## Optional validation

Compare the original probe's banking trace against an equivalently configured openMSX mapper if available. Record profile differences without treating them as universal hardware behavior.

## Required post-merge verification

None
